identity.title: Observations of solar chromospheric oscillations at 3 mm with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We used ALMA observations of the quiet Sun described by Nindos et al. (2018).

targets.name: Quiet Sun, targets 2-7 (mu = 0.34-1) along position angle 135 deg

question.value: Characterize spatially-resolved chromospheric oscillations of the quiet Sun at 3 mm, their center-to-limb variation, and their lag relative to AIA 1600 Å

evidence.quote: To study spatially-resolved chromospheric oscillations of the quiet Sun in the mm-domain at a resolution of a few arcsec, typically 2.4$''$$\times$4.5$''$.
seven 120$^{"}$ circular fields of view (targets) were observed at 3 mm (100 GHz) on March 16, 2017.
for all targets was 2.4$''$$\times$4.5$''$, with the exception of target 7 where the resolution was 2.3$''$$\times$8.1$''$.
Each target was observed for 10 minutes with a 2-s cadence.
The observations were performed on March 16, 2017

provided.value: 1600 Å and 304 Å image sequences for comparison and time-lag analysis

evidence.quote: We also analyzed AIA images at 1600 and 304 Å, convolved with the ALMA resolution

what.value: Reduced ALMA 3 mm quiet-Sun image sequences (targets, solar rotation correction, reduction)

evidence.quote: More details regarding the reduction of the ALMA data can be found in Nindos et al. (2018).

evidence.quote: we submitted the resulting average images to the masking procedure described in Nindos et al. (2018).

method.value: Extract central 80"x80" region of each target; degrade AIA to ALMA resolution; correct differential rotation; co-align by cross-correlating time-averaged images

evidence.quote: We extracted a 80$''$$\times$80$''$ region from the original 120$''$ diameter FoV at the center of each target

method.value: Pixels below (above) a second-degree 2D polynomial fit of the average image are cell (network)

evidence.quote: Pixels with values smaller (larger) than these of the mask are tagged as cell (network) pixels.
it though leads to satisfactory results as judged by visual inspection of the resulting masks and the actual average images.

method.value: Subtract 3rd-degree polynomial from each pixel light curve, Fourier transform, average PSDs over FoV, cell and network

evidence.quote: We then calculated the PSDs for every pixel in the FoV and averaged over the entire FoV, as well as the cell and network using the masks described above.
The frequency resolution of all three data sets, determined by the duration of the time series, is 1.7 mHz.

validation.value: Compared with subtraction of mean only; polynomial degrees 1-4 tested

evidence.quote: experimentation with different degree polynomials (i.e., 1-4) showed that the higher the degree of the polynomial, the smaller the amplitude of the peak around the p-mode domain.

method.value: Fit linear background plus log-normal peak; derive peak frequency a3 and rms from integral

method.value: Pixel-to-pixel cross-correlation with region growing, clusters with coefficient above 0.7

evidence.quote: we determined clusters of pixels with cross-correlation coefficient above 0.7 and counted the number of pixels per cluster.

analysis_steps.goal: ALMA-AIA time lag and formation height difference

method.value: Cross-correlate light curves averaged over 3"x3" macropixels, keep max coefficient >= 0.7, parabolic fit of peak for lag; height from lag times sound speed

evidence.quote: The optimal temporal lag was calculated from a parabolic fitting of the cross-correlation function around its peak.

assumptions.value: Upward sound waves at about 12 km/s (7000 K)

evidence.quote: traveling at a speed of $\approx$ 12 $\mathrm{km{s}^{-1}}$ (i.e., corresponding to a temperature of 7000 K)

validation.value: Argued lag is real despite differing peak frequencies

evidence.quote: We may thus safely conclude that the time lag is real.

findings_qualitative.value: Oscillation coherence length is comparable to the ALMA resolution (about 4")

evidence.quote: The coherence length-scale of the oscillations is commensurate with the spatial resolution of our ALMA observations.

claims.hypothesis: Are p-mode oscillations present at 3 mm in cell and network?
claims.experiment: PSD analysis of ALMA light curves with log-normal peak fits
claims.result: Peak at 4.2 mHz, rms about 55-75 K (about 1% of Tb)
claims.finding: Omnipresent p-mode oscillations in cell and network, with a moderate center-to-limb increase

evidence.quote: p-mode oscillations at 3 mm are omnipresent in both network and cell with frequencies of $4.2 \pm 1.7$ mHz

claims.hypothesis: What is the formation-height difference between ALMA 3 mm and AIA 1600 Å?
claims.finding: About 1200 km height difference assuming upward sound waves

evidence.quote: ALMA 3 mm lags AIA 1600 Å by $\sim100$ s

claims.hypothesis: Are oscillations fully resolved by lower-resolution BIMA data?

evidence.quote: chromospheric oscillations in the mm-domain are not fully resolved at a resolution comparable to the length-scale of the network

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Power-law background not used because the 10-min series are too short

evidence.loc: 2.3 Fitting of spatially averaged power spectra
evidence.quote: the short duration of the analyzed sequences per target (i.e., $\sim$ 10 min), does not allow to extend the PSDs to significantly lower frequencies

limitations_admitted.value: 10-min series limit frequency resolution to 1.7 mHz and prevent detecting longer-period oscillations; rms values are upper limits due to detrending

evidence.quote: the derived p-mode rms amplitudes from the use of a 3rd degree polynomial fitting of the original light-curves could be seen as upper limits.

referee_caveats_inferred: Height difference depends on assumed sound speed and on 1600 Å temperature dependence
Lag assumes similar wave-propagation phase in both channels; a 1.7 mHz frequency resolution is coarse
